finalText:
Migration is complete. 36 call sites across 12 files converted to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

All files parse clean under `node --check`. `db.query` now has zero first-party callers.

Two things I deliberately did **not** change:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` (2 calls) — still on `db.query`.** Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade, with local edits silently lost. Patching it would be reverted by the next upgrade, and it's the one place `db.query` genuinely still needs to exist. So `lib/db.js` can't drop the deprecated method yet. Resolving that is an upstream-or-replace decision rather than a sweep edit — worth flagging as the remaining blocker if the plan is to delete `query` before the driver's next major.

- **`cache.query(...)` (~20 call sites).** Despite the matching name, that's `lib/cache.js` — it takes a cache key, not SQL, and is unrelated to this migration.

One note on the new form: `execute` also accepts a `timeoutMs` option, which was the stated reason the positional form couldn't carry per-call options. I did a mechanical translation and set it nowhere, so behaviour is unchanged — if any of these queries wanted a timeout, that's a follow-up.
